brief: RBC's global rates update: central banks are hiking to prevent energy-price inflation from passing into wages (second-round effects). RBA is probably done (post-GFC high 4.85%, split 6-3 vote), with a cut seen late 2027. RBC flags underpriced risk of one more hike before mid-2027, though not in December. ECB has hiked 50bp and should deliver one more in December, reaching a 2.75% terminal and stopping there absent wage transmission, which it sees little of yet. BoE hiked 25bp in November, more hawkish than expected (Mann dissented for 50bp). RBC now expects another 25bp in February, then a long hold. Market pricing (SONIA) implies roughly three more hikes, which RBC calls unrealizable, setting up Gilt outperformance. Fed sees high odds of back-to-back Dec/January hikes or a quarterly pace beyond March, with low odds of stopping before removing the remaining 50bp of last year's insurance cuts, driven by stable labor markets and hot inflation data despite equity weakness. BoC should hike again in December toward its long-held 3.25% terminal, barring softer Oct CPI, Q3 GDP, or Nov jobs data. Yields: flat-to-higher into Q1, then stable-to-lower, except the UK.
